ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant screening of all UBOs, general partners, and authorized signatories against: (1) the UN Consolidated List (UNSC Res 1373 and 1988); (2) Canadian sanctions lists maintained under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act ('Sergei Magnitsky Law'); (3) the OFAC SDN List as United States best practice given CUSMA trade integration; (4) the World Bank and MDB debarment lists; and (5) domestic and foreign PEP databases covering heads of state, senior political officials, senior judicial officials, and senior military officers. Screening is exact-match on alias/transliteration variants, re-run at inception, upon any material ownership change, and every 90 days. For the Medium_Risk_Enhanced agrochemical commodity tier, Enhanced Due Diligence requires source-of-funds verification and written beneficial-ownership attestations prior to any Swift LC or wire transfer onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises: https://registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (online 'Reservation of a name' service)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal denomination of a Quebec limited partnership must be in French. A non-French version may be used only if a French version is already registered or the name is a registered trademark under the Trademarks Act. Names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters for the public file. The name must include the designation 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' may be disclosed only as an auxiliary English-language version. All registration filings with the REQ must be drafted in French.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No automatic extension is available; upon expiry the applicant must file a new reservation request for the same or an amended name. If the REQ rejects the proposed name, the applicant must, within 30 days of the notice of refusal, submit a written reconsideration request to the Direction de l'immatriculation of the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, quoting the reservation file number, providing a certified French translation of any foreign supporting documents, and attaching trademark registration evidence if the exception is invoked. Should the Registraire maintain the refusal, the applicant may file a motion to institute proceedings for judicial review before the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (TAQ) within 60 days of the second refusal, and thereafter may appeal to the Court of Quebec.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure post-office box or virtual mail-forwarding address is rejected by the REQ. A commercial domiciliation service is permissible only if it maintains a physical office in Quebec where the declared responsible natural person is physically present for service of process and where the REQ verification teams can attend. For the Medium_Risk_Enhanced fertilizer-wholesale tier, banking counterparties will treat the domiciliation arrangement as an Enhanced Due Diligence trigger and require sublease or service agreements evidencing real control over the premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% - 40% within the first 18 months of registration, driven by (i) the REQ's targeted audit and 'verification of establishments' program for partnerships with foreign general partners; (ii) FINTRAC examination probabilities that rise with Swift LC and cross-border wire volume; and (iii) periodic bank-conducted on-site verification required by correspondent-banking compliance policies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236–2269 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 7, 19–23, 32; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1), ss. 2–7.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), operated through the Revenu Québec online portal ('clicSÉQUR Entreprises')
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'inscription / Declaration of Registration for a société en commandite (limited partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None — Québec law imposes no minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for limited partnerships. The Declaration of Registration must state the aggregate amount of limited partners' contributions, which may be in cash or in kind, as agreed under arts. 2242–2247 CCQ.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the first resolution of the General Partner of [●] Limited Partnership: (1) the Limited Partnership Agreement submitted is approved and adopted, and each Limited Partner is authorized to execute it and subscribe for the designated Partnership Units; (2) the aggregate Limited Partner contributions, CAD [●], are accepted and shall be stated in the Declaration of Registration; (3) the head office is fixed at [●], Province of Québec; (4) the General Partner is appointed managing partner; (5) the General Partner is authorized to sign and file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, appoint counsel, and open banking accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name search and reservation module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a request for name research and reservation ('demande de réservation de nom') through the REQ portal. The proposed name must include the legal element 'société en commandite' or 'Limited Partnership', comply with the distinctiveness rules of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, and avoid prohibited or confusing terms. Upon approval, the REQ issues a certificate of reservation valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Authorization of the General Partner to reserve the name
Identity and jurisdiction details of the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an amended name compliant with the registrar's name standards; a formal review may be requested from the registrar within 60 days, followed by judicial review before the Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Internal Constitution: Limited Partnership Agreement and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel or notary engaged by the partners; no state filing at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement governed by arts. 2236–2269 CCQ, fixing the head office in Québec, identifying the General Partner and the limited partners, defining Partnership Units, and recording contributions. Adopt the pro forma First Resolution of the General Partner covering the agreement, contributions, head office, managing partner appointment, and filing authorities. Prepare executed powers of attorney for any agent that will file with the REQ.
required_dossiers: First Resolution of the General Partner
Nominations of managing partner and officers
Powers of attorney for filing agents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any defects in the partnership agreement or powers of attorney prior to filing; re-execute documents if partner identity or contribution amounts are inaccurate; non-resident partners must verify legal capacity and documentary formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online filing via clicSÉQUR Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration for the limited partnership online, completing all mandatory fields: enterprise name; head office address in Québec; identification of the General Partner and each limited partner; aggregate amount of limited partner contributions; duration; and principal activity (NAICS 424910). Pay the approximate CAD 36 filing fee. If the General Partner is not resident in Québec, designate a natural person resident in Québec for service of documents. Download the acknowledgement upon filing.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney to the filing agent
General Partner resolution authorizing the filing
Partnership agreement (kept at head office; not filed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The REQ issues a notice of refusal for incomplete submissions, granting 30 days to remedy or the application lapses; resubmit the corrected declaration without additional fees where filed in time; contested refusals are reviewable by the registrar and thereafter by the Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance: Certificate, NEQ, and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; Revenu Québec for tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, download the 'Attestation d'immatriculation' (registration certificate) from the REQ portal and obtain the NEQ (Québec enterprise number). Open a partnership bank account using the certificate, partnership agreement, and First Resolution; establish the register of partners and minute book at the head office; prepare the partnership's annual declaration calendar; register for GST/HST with the CRA and QST with Revenu Québec as applicable to the pass-through entity.
required_dossiers: First Resolution of the General Partner
Proof of Québec head office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or register data contains errors, file a 'demande de modification' (amendment) with the REQ for correction, effective retroactively; ensure the annual declaration is filed before the statutory deadline to avoid dissolution or administrative strike-off.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP); local municipality with territorial jurisdiction; Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) for physical premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating permit is required for the wholesale trading activity itself; a municipal building occupancy permit and, where a physical warehouse is operated, a conditional environmental authorization under s. 22 of the Environment Quality Act may apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full environmental impact assessment for wholesale distribution; a ministerial declaration of conformity or municipal authorization may be required only where the warehouse construction or operation presents a measurable environmental risk (e.g., new construction exceeding the regulatory threshold under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulation).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent is expected from the wholesale activity; any sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer by-laws and the Regulation respecting municipal wastewater treatment works (CQLR c Q-2, r. 34.1). Air emissions from urea/prilled product handling must respect the Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 4.1), including a 20% opacity limit for fugitive dust; GHG reporting obligations apply under the Regulation respecting mandatory reporting of certain emissions of contaminants if emissions reach the statutory trigger; hazardous waste handling, if any, must follow the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of residual materials (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire prevention service and an RBQ occupancy permit under the Building Act (CQLR c B-1.1) and Québec Construction Code; structural load inspection for any fertilizer storage warehouse; CNESST workplace health and safety clearance, WHMIS (SIMDUT) training, and safety data sheets for urea and potassium chloride, including combustible-dust control measures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Revenu Québec (for GST/HST and QST registration in Quebec); CRA portal: My Business Account; Revenu Québec portal: Clic Revenu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada must register for a CRA Business Number (BN) and, if engaged in taxable activities in Quebec, register with Revenu Québec for a QST number. Application can be made online, by mail, or via authorized representative. The partnership must appoint a representative for service in Canada if it is a non-resident partnership. Registration must occur before filing returns or remitting taxes; GST/HST and QST registrations are effective from the date the entity commences commercial activity, subject to the small supplier threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A partnership is not a taxpayer for federal income tax purposes; each partner reports share of income. For GST/HST, a partnership is treated as a person and must register if taxable supplies exceed $30,000; a non-resident partnership may elect to register voluntarily. Quebec QST rules mirror GST/HST with certain differences; a partnership may elect to have Revenu Québec qualify its provincial election where permitted. Check-the-box elections are not applicable under Canadian law; however, hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act may impose entity characterization adjustments, and a Canadian partnership can elect to make certain fiscal period selections (e.g., non-calendar fiscal year) that affect deferral.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies over four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST; the QST threshold corresponds to the same $30,000 threshold applicable to taxable supplies in Quebec, subject to Revenu Québec rules
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate a real-time e-invoicing clearance system; electronic invoicing is authorized but must contain prescribed information. Quebec mandates the use of the Revenu Québec digital attestation and standardized electronic form for QST registrants. There is no national real-time tax stamping or API clearance requirement similar to certain Latin American jurisdictions; however, businesses must report prescribed information through the CRA's GST/HST NETFILE for electronic filings and via Revenu Québec's electronic filing services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated under GST/HST and QST applies to supplies of goods that are exported by the vendor, including sales of fertilizer products sold to non-residents for export provided the vendor retains evidence of export. A supply of goods is zero-rated where the goods are delivered by the vendor to a common carrier for export, or shipped to a destination outside Canada, and the supplier has satisfactory documentary evidence that the goods were exported. Services performed on goods destined for export may also be zero-rated if the service is performed for a non-resident. The export of goods by a licensed customs broker under the sales contract qualifies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A / Canadian Automated Export Declaration - CAED)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of payment from foreign buyer
Sales invoice and contract demonstrating the goods were sold for export
Customs entry or release documentation in the importing jurisdiction (where available)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or misleading export claims give rise to penalties under the Excise Tax Act, including penalties equal to 5% of the net tax falsely reported plus up to 20% of the amounts claimed in respect of non-compliance. CRA may reassess an input tax credit or zero-rated treatment at any time within the normal reassessment period of four years, with extended periods for misrepresentation. Revenu Québec imposes parallel penalties under the Taxation Act, including 5% plus 20% administrative penalties for false QST claims; criminal prosecution is possible for intentional evasion. The CRA may deny zero-rated treatment retroactively and assess net tax, interest, and penalties if the exporter cannot substantiate the export with required documentation within the stipulated retention period of six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); responsibility for monetary policy and the national payment system. Canada does not maintain a distinct Foreign Exchange Administration; exchange controls and cross-border capital regulations are administered under the Bank of Canada Act, the Currency Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, with the Department of Finance Canada holding policy authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no exchange control restrictions on current account transactions or capital account transactions, including inbound capital injections, trade finance settlements, and profit remittances. A Quebec limited partnership may freely receive foreign currency and convert to CAD at any authorized bank. The principal hurdle on outbound distributions to non-resident partners is Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act on amounts allocated to non-residents, typically at 25% absent a tax treaty reduction; repatriation of contributed capital is unrestricted. Banks may require completion of a non-resident declaration and tax form to confirm treaty eligibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio. A Quebec-based LP engaged in wholesale urea and potash trade may retain export receipts in USD or other currencies. Transactions of CAD 10,000 or more are reported to FINTRAC by the financial intermediary as an electronic funds transfer report. Exports are also subject to record-keeping obligations under the Customs Act and Canada Border Services Agency reporting, but no CAD conversion is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account; Multi-Currency USD/CAD Account; Import Documentary Credit Facility
Operating Account; Capital Escrow/Trust Account; Trade Finance and FX Settlement Account
Operating Account; USD Correspondent Clearing Account; Commercial Letter of Credit Facility
Global Transaction Banking Account; Cross-Border USD/CAD Sweep
Operating Account; Business Cash Management and EDI Payment Solution

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for ancillary treasury flows only. Canadian law does not recognize EU Electronic Money Institution (EMI) passporting. Fintech payment firms such as Wise and Airwallex may operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) in Canada and must be registered with FINTRAC. They are viable for low-value payment aggregation, cross-border vendor payments, and FX execution at mid-market rates, but they cannot issue Canadian-dollar deposit accounts, provide regulated commercial credit, or issue documentary letters of credit. The primary clearing rails for fertilizer commodity trade must remain with Tier-1 domestic commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Quebec Tier-1 banks generally mandate physical presence for at least one authorized representative, usually the general partner or a director of the corporate general partner, for non-resident or medium-risk clients. Remote account opening using audio-video KYC is accepted only in narrow cases, and a resident Canadian compliance representative may be required to attend an in-person interview. The Bank Secrecy Act equivalent in Canada, the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, does not statutorily require physical appearance, but bank internal policies impose enhanced due diligence, including an in-person meeting at a Quebec branch, verification of the registered office, and direct confirmation of beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners creating an opaque beneficial ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized LP agreement, Quebec Registraire des entreprises certificate of registration, proof of appointment of the general partner, complete organizational chart identifying all ultimate beneficial owners with 25% or more direct or indirect interest, government-issued identification, source-of-wealth narrative, and a reference letter from each partner's home-country bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fertilizer commodity exposure flagged for possible diversion to dual-use chemical production
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed end-use certificate and attestation from downstream purchasers, customer due-dediligence questionnaire, ISO 9001 quality assurance records, bill of lading and commercial invoice tracing the shipment to licensed agricultural storage, and confirmation that no party is listed under the Canadian Sanctions Regulations or OFAC/UN screening lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected wire value significantly above CAD 10,000, triggering large transaction reporting to FINTRAC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying sales contract or purchase order, proforma invoice, packing list, proof of commodity ownership, beneficial ownership declaration, and a board/general partner resolution authorizing the transaction. The bank will file the FINTRAC report; the client must maintain a complete audit trail for seven years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the registered head office and physical operating location of the limited partnership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement or virtual office service agreement for the Quebec registered address, letters confirming the general partner's operational base, site visit photographs if requested, and an organizational narrative proving the registered agent relationship is compliant with the Quebec Civil Code.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident partners must be wired via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the LP's CAD operating account held at a Canadian Tier-1 bank. CAD-denominated large-value transfers settle in real time on the Payments Canada Lynx system; USD-denominated injections clear through correspondent banking arrangements or via CLS for same-day FX. The wire beneficiary field must include the LP legal name, Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), the phrase 'capital contribution', and must not indicate a taxable purchase. FINTRAC EFT reporting will apply to transactions of CAD 10,000 or more; the bank will verify the source of funds against the LP agreement and beneficial ownership register.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of urea and potash imports, the preferred outbound clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for outright telegraphic transfer. For deferred payment or guarantee of delivery, issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700 under UCP600, with confirming bank participation as requested. USD-denominated payments may be routed through the bank's USD clearing accounts or CHIPS; CAD payments use the Lynx high-value system. All instructions must include the commercial invoice, weight certificate, port of loading, and bill of lading. Freight payment may be routed separately via SWIFT MT103 with a distinct purpose code.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards between CAD and USD or EUR executed under ISDA/CSA documentation with a Schedule I Canadian bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing liquid emerging-market currencies, provided the LP holds a matching physical trade exposure
Cross-currency swaps for USD/CAD principal conversion and interest re-pricing under a bilateral ISDA agreement
Vanilla and barrier FX options transacted with a CIRO-member derivatives dealer and cleared in Canada where applicable
Natural hedging through multi-currency operating accounts offsetting USD receivables against USD payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) pursuant to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (s. 83)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year on or before 15 June; the transmission window opens on the partnership's registration anniversary date, with the first declaration deferrable to the next 15 June when initial registration occurs after that date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 200 applied by REQ together with a statutory monetary penalty of CAD 200 to CAD 3,000; failure to regularize after formal notice leads to administrative radiation (strike-off) of the partnership registration and loss of legal-publicity opposability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500) plus arrears interest; inaccurate reporting can trigger reassessment of all partners under ITA s. 96 and, for knowing omissions, penalties up to CAD 200,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period, aligned with the federal T5013 due calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties and interest under the Tax Administration Act (Québec), including late-filing penalties of 10% of unpaid amounts or CAD 200 to CAD 1,000 for omitted prescribed returns, and possible attribution of undisclosed allocations to the general partner.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer payroll information returns (T4 Summary / RL-1) - applicable only if the partnership employs staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T4 Summary by the last day of February following the calendar year; RL-1/RL-3 summaries by the last day of February of the following year.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit obligation is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership by the Civil Code of Quebec or Canadian tax legislation. An independent audit becomes compulsory when: (i) the partnership agreement or a unanimous partner resolution mandates audited financial statements; (ii) a lender, insurer, or fertilizer-supply contract requires a certified audit; (iii) the partnership qualifies as a 'reporting partnership' under the federal Income Tax Act (more than five members, a corporate or partnership member, gross revenue above CAD 2,000,000, or total assets above CAD 5,000,000) and CRA or Revenu Québec formally requires audited statements; or (iv) a statutory audit demand is issued under the Tax Administration Act (Québec) or ITA s. 231.6.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS applies where the partnership is required to be a publicly accountable enterprise; otherwise Canadian ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook - Canadian GAAP) is the default framework, with income computed under GAAP and adjusted for the partnership allocation rules of ITA s. 96 and the Taxation Act (Québec).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration operates as an annual confirmation: the general partner must verify and report the name, address, and participation of every general and limited partner, thereby capturing any partnership-interest transfer effected in the preceding year; where no transfer occurred, the filed declaration stands as a negative confirmation. Quebec maintains no public central UBO registry for LPs, but the federal Corporate Transparency Act (Bill C-42) will require the partnership to keep current individuals-with-significant-control records and disclose them on lawful request; the LP must therefore maintain an internal UBO register reconciled at least annually with the REQ declaration.
